title: Warp-weighted loom
summary: On a warp-weighted loom the threads hang from a beam between two upright posts, and bundles of them are pulled straight by loom weights of fired clay or stone. The weaver works from the top downwards, beating each row up into the cloth, and twills woven this way were prized for blankets and cloaks.
howToPlay: Pick a wool colour from the hanks and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other half of the cloth.
Copy the blanket shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The cloth is mirrored left and right, so every shape you weave is also woven on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its wool colour both match the blanket you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: The upright weighted loom was used across ancient Europe, Scandinavia and the Mediterranean, and clay and stone loom weights are common finds on old settlements. In parts of the North Atlantic it stayed in use for twill cloth into modern times.
